title: Array
text: An array stores elements in contiguous memory, so reading by index takes constant time O(1), while inserting in the middle costs O(n) because later elements must shift.

title: Linked List
text: A linked list stores each element in a node that points to the next node. Insertion at a known position is O(1), but searching for a value takes O(n) since nodes are scattered.

title: Hash Table
text: A hash table turns a key into a bucket index with a hash function. With a reasonable load factor, lookup is O(1) on average; collisions are handled by chaining or open addressing.

title: Red-Black Tree
text: A red-black tree is a self-balancing binary search tree. Rotations and recoloring keep its height logarithmic, which guarantees O(log n) search, insertion and deletion.

title: Quicksort
text: Quicksort partitions an array around a pivot and recurses on both sides. Average time is O(n log n), but an unlucky pivot degrades it to O(n^2).

title: Merge Sort
text: Merge sort splits the array in half, sorts each half recursively, then merges the two sorted halves. It always runs in O(n log n) and needs O(n) extra space.

title: Dijkstra
text: Dijkstra's algorithm finds the shortest path from a source vertex to every other vertex in a weighted graph with non-negative edges, using a priority queue to pick the nearest unvisited vertex.

title: Bellman-Ford
text: Bellman-Ford relaxes every edge V-1 times, so it tolerates negative weights and detects negative cycles, at a cost of O(V E) time.

title: Topological Sort
text: Topological sort orders the vertices of a directed acyclic graph so that every edge points from an earlier vertex to a later one. Kahn's algorithm finishes it in O(V+E).

title: Amortized Analysis
text: A dynamic array doubles its capacity when full, so appending n elements costs O(n) in total, which is an amortized O(1) per append.
